intended_object: For two points P, Q in the upper half-plane with different real parts, the point c on the real axis that is the centre of the semicircle through P and Q, i.e. the unique real c with |P − c| = |Q − c|. This semicircle is the hyperbolic geodesic through P and Q. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The centre c must satisfy |P − c|² = |Q − c|². Expanding gives |P|² − 2c·Re P = |Q|² − 2c·Re Q, so c = (|Q|² − |P|²) / (2(Re Q − Re P)). That is exactly the body of the definition. When Re P = Re Q, Lean's division by zero makes the value 0. The docstring rules this case out ("when `P.re ≠ Q.re`"), so this is only the usual junk value. The library proves what the docstring promises: `normSq_sub_circleCenter` shows the centre is equidistant from P and Q, and `circleCenter_eq_of_normSq_eq` shows it is the only such point on the real axis. Mathlib has no definition of this centre. The notion belongs to the upper half-plane model of hyperbolic geometry, so ℍ is its natural setting and the definition is not too narrow.
